newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close with slight gain.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close with slight gain.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed slightly higher after drifting in a narrow band Thursday and were seen staying rangebound, dealers said.
"The market will probably move sideways tomorrow unless the U.S. jobs report causes a major swing on Wall Street," said Nestor de Cessare at traders Allaria Ledesma.
The blue-chip MerVal index erased early losses and added 0.3 percent to close at 850.03, stretching gains so far this week to 1.1 percent.
"Business was very selective and favored some stocks which were underperforming the rest of the market," de Cessare said.

Among the laggards which rebounded were foods giant Molinos and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, up 2.8 percent, 3.5 percent respectively, and to a lesser degree steelmaker Acindar, up 0.4 percent.

"The bolsa is regrouping and we may see a trading lull until company results start streaming in next week," another broker said. "Otherwise fundamentals here remain strong and the bulls are still setting the pace in New York, especially in the Treasuries market."
The broad market inched up 0.2 percent, with winners outpacing losers 36 to 25 and 17 issues closing flat.
Floor volume eased to 28.8 million pesos from 32.4 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover slowed to 92.5 million pesos from 111.3 million Wednesday.

Traders noted carmakers were among the top MerVal losers, with Ciadea down 2.5 percent and Sevel off 1.6 percent. They linked the drop to the leadership change in Brazil's Central Bank, as new chief Gustavo Franco favors a tight trade policy which could hurt Argentine exports.
Other heavy losers were cement stock Juan Minetti and Banco Frances, off 2.4 percent and 1.7 percent, respectively.
